sop:
Please set up a daily reminder automation to send out emails to our members reminding them of their upcoming renewal date. This should start at 11:00 AM every day, and we want to send a reminder to everyone whose renewal date is tomorrow and who are currently active members. The email should say: "Hi [Member Name], a reminder from the gym: your renewal date is tomorrow."

Please ensure that no more than 30 emails are sent in a batch, and that these emails only go out between 7:30 AM and 7:00 PM. If the batch needs to be sent, I will approve it within 1 hour and review up to 5 previews before approving. No one should receive more than 150 messages per day. Let everyone know if the batch isn't approved so we can adjust accordingly.
policy:
policy GymPolicy {
  allow read Members(name, email, renews_on, status, health_notes)
  allow contact Members.email
  deny reveal Members.health_notes
  limit sends 150 per day
  send only between 07:30 and 19:00
  approval batch valid 1 hour max 30 preview 5
}
sheets: sheet Members "Members" { name: Text, email: Email, renews_on: Date, status: Text, dues: Money, health_notes: Text private }
program:
procedure GymRenewalDateReminders {
  about "Remind each member about their renewal date"
  policy GymPolicy
  sheet Members "Members" { name: Text, email: Email, renews_on: Date, status: Text, dues: Money, health_notes: Text private }
  trigger every day at 11:00

  let all = fetch Members
  let due = filter all where renews_on == today() + 1 day and status == "active"
  let msgs = draft each r in due up to 30 email to r.email subject "Your renewal date tomorrow": "Hi {r.name}, a reminder from the gym: your renewal date is tomorrow."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 1 day else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

The system should send a reminder email at 4:00 PM daily, but only to those who haven't picked up their watches yet and haven’t cancelled the service.   allow read Watches(owner, email, ready_on, status)
  allow contact Watches.email
  deny reveal Watches.serial_number
  limit sends 100 per day
  send only between 07:30 and 19:00
  approval batch valid 1 hour max 20 preview 5
}
sheets: sheet Watches "Watches" { owner: Text, email: Email, ready_on: Date, status: Text, quote: Money, serial_number: Text private }
program:
procedure WatchesWinBack {
  about "Nudge owners whose watch repair was long ago"
  policy WatchesPolicy
  sheet Watches "Watches" { owner: Text, email: Email, ready_on: Date, status: Text, quote: Money, serial_number: Text private }
  trigger every day at 16:00

  let all = fetch Watches
  let old = filter all where days_between(ready_on, today()) >= 42 and status != "cancelled"
  let oldest = sort old by ready_on first 20
  let msgs = draft each r in oldest up to 20 email to r.email subject "We miss you": "Hi {r.owner default 'there'}, it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the shop."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 12 hours else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

sop: Please create an automation that sends a welcome email to new students and follows up after 7 days if they haven't completed their session. The welcome email should be sent between 7:30 AM and 7 PM and no more than 150 emails should be sent per day. Only the owner should approve and review both the welcome and follow-up emails. If a student has already been contacted or their status is marked as "done" or "cancelled," the process should stop.

  allow read Students(student, parent_email, status, learning_notes)
  allow write Students(status)
  allow contact Students.parent_email
  deny reveal Students.learning_notes
  limit sends 150 per day
  send only between 07:30 and 19:00
}
sheets: sheet Students "Students" { student: Text, parent_email: Email, next_session: DateTime, status: Text, balance: Money, learning_notes: Text private }
program:
procedure TutoringFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new student, then follow up once"
  policy TutoringPolicy
  sheet Students "Students" { student: Text, parent_email: Email, next_session: DateTime, status: Text, balance: Money, learning_notes: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Students

  let first = draft email to r.parent_email subject "Welcome": "Hi {r.student}, thanks for choosing the center! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 7 days
  let all = fetch Students
  let now_r = find all where parent_email == r.parent_email else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "done" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft email to now_r.parent_email subject "Checking in": "Hi {now_r.student default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

  sheet Families "Families" { parent: Text, email: Email, due_date: Date, status: Text, balance: Money, health_notes: Text private }

- When a new visit is added, send a welcome message to the patient: "Hi [Patient Name], thanks for choosing the clinic! Reply with any questions." This message should be sent within 6 hours and require my approval.
- After 5 days, send a check-in message to the same patient: "Hi [Patient Name], just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?" This also needs my approval within 6 hours.
- Only send these messages between 7:30 AM and 7:00 PM.
- Do not share the patient's diagnosis.
- Limit the total number of messages sent to 150 per day.

Let me know if you have any questions or need more information.
policy:
policy ClinicPolicy {
  allow read Visits(patient, phone, status)
  allow write Visits(status)
  allow contact Visits.phone
  deny reveal Visits.diagnosis
  limit sends 150 per day
  send only between 07:30 and 19:00
}
sheets: sheet Visits "Visits" { patient: Text, phone: Phone, starts: DateTime, status: Text, copay: Money, diagnosis: Text private }
program:
procedure ClinicFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new patient, then follow up once"
  policy ClinicPolicy
  sheet Visits "Visits" { patient: Text, phone: Phone, starts: DateTime, status: Text, copay: Money, diagnosis: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Visits

  let first = draft sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.patient}, thanks for choosing the clinic! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 5 days
  let all = fetch Visits
  let now_r = find all where phone == r.phone else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "done" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft sms to now_r.phone: "Hi {now_r.patient default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

sop: Could you please set up an automated system to nudge swimmers whose pass has expired for over 30 days? The system should only send emails between 8 AM and 8 PM. It should not include any health information and must be limited to sending out 150 messages per day. Please send the emails at 6 PM daily. I need to approve batches of up to 15 messages at a time with a maximum wait time of 1 hour before deciding, or the process will stop. Could you ensure that the emails are drafts until I give my approval? Thank you!
policy:
policy PoolPolicy {
  allow read SwimPasses(swimmer, email, expires_on, status)
  allow contact SwimPasses.email
  deny reveal SwimPasses.health_flags
  limit sends 150 per day
  send only between 08:00 and 20:00
  approval batch valid 1 hour max 15 preview 5
}
sheets: sheet SwimPasses "SwimPasses" { swimmer: Text, email: Email, expires_on: Date, status: Text, fee: Money, health_flags: Text private }
program:
procedure PoolWinBack {
  about "Nudge swimmers whose pass expiry was long ago"
  policy PoolPolicy
  sheet SwimPasses "SwimPasses" { swimmer: Text, email: Email, expires_on: Date, status: Text, fee: Money, health_flags: Text private }
  trigger every day at 18:00

  let all = fetch SwimPasses
  let old = filter all where days_between(expires_on, today()) >= 30 and status != "cancelled"
  let oldest = sort old by expires_on first 15
  let msgs = draft each r in oldest up to 15 email to r.email subject "We miss you": "Hi {r.swimmer}, it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the pool."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

sop:
Please set up an automation to follow up with new customers after they schedule a pickup. Here’s what I need:

- Send the first message, "Hi [Customer Name], thanks for choosing our service! Reply with any questions." to the customer’s phone number within 2 hours.
- Approve the message before sending it.
- Set the customer status to "contacted" after sending the first message.
- Wait 5 days and then send a follow-up message, "Hi [Customer Name], just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?" if they haven’t picked up yet.
- Approve this follow-up message before sending it.
- Only send messages between 8 AM and 6 PM.
- Limit the daily message count to 100.
- The system should not share the gate code with anyone.
- Ensure all messages are sent during working hours.
policy:
policy JunkPolicy {
  allow read Pickups(customer, phone, status, gate_code)
  allow write Pickups(status)
  allow contact Pickups.phone
  deny reveal Pickups.gate_code
  limit sends 100 per day
  send only between 08:00 and 18:00
}
sheets: sheet Pickups "Pickups" { customer: Text, phone: Phone, pickup_at: DateTime, status: Text, price: Money, gate_code: Text private }
program:
procedure JunkFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new customer, then follow up once"
  policy JunkPolicy
  sheet Pickups "Pickups" { customer: Text, phone: Phone, pickup_at: DateTime, status: Text, price: Money, gate_code: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Pickups

  let first = draft sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.customer default 'there'}, thanks for choosing the service! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 5 days
  let all = fetch Pickups
  let now_r = find all where phone == r.phone else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "done" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft sms to now_r.phone: "Hi {now_r.customer default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

sop: Could you set up an automation that emails students who haven't attended a glass class in over 90 days? The emails should be sent every morning at 9 AM, but no more than 15 emails per day. Only send these emails between 7:30 AM and 7 PM. Please ask for my approval before sending any messages. Limit approvals to a 30-minute window, with a maximum of 5 previews at once. policy GlassPolicy {
  allow read Classes(student, email, class_at, status, burn_notes)
  allow contact Classes.email
  deny reveal Classes.burn_notes
  limit sends 150 per day
  send only between 07:30 and 19:00
  approval batch valid 30 minutes max 15 preview 5
}
sheets: sheet Classes "Classes" { student: Text, email: Email, class_at: DateTime, status: Text, fee: Money, burn_notes: Text private }
program:
procedure GlassWinBack {
  about "Nudge students whose glass class was long ago"
  policy GlassPolicy
  sheet Classes "Classes" { student: Text, email: Email, class_at: DateTime, status: Text, fee: Money, burn_notes: Text private }
  trigger every day at 09:00

  let all = fetch Classes
  let old = filter all where days_between(class_at, today()) >= 90 and status != "cancelled"
  let oldest = sort old by class_at first 15
  let msgs = draft each r in oldest up to 15 email to r.email subject "We miss you": "Hi {r.student default 'there'}, it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the studio."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 12 hours else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

sop: Please set up an automation to remind members about their renewal dates. The reminders should be sent daily at 5:30 PM, but no more than 20 emails at a time. Only active members whose renewal dates are tomorrow should receive these emails. No one should see the health notes, and the emails should be sent between 7:30 AM and 7:00 PM. Only the gym owner should approve the batch of emails, with a maximum of 20 previews allowed and the approval needing to happen within 30 minutes. No more than 50 emails should be sent in a day. Thank you!
policy:
policy GymPolicy {
  allow read Members(name, email, renews_on, status, health_notes)
  allow contact Members.email
  deny reveal Members.health_notes
  limit sends 50 per day
  send only between 07:30 and 19:00
  approval batch valid 30 minutes max 20 preview 5
}
sheets: sheet Members "Members" { name: Text, email: Email, renews_on: Date, status: Text, dues: Money, health_notes: Text private }
program:
procedure GymRenewalDateReminders {
  about "Remind each member about their renewal date"
  policy GymPolicy
  sheet Members "Members" { name: Text, email: Email, renews_on: Date, status: Text, dues: Money, health_notes: Text private }
  trigger every day at 17:30

  let all = fetch Members
  let due = filter all where renews_on == today() + 1 day and status == "active"
  let msgs = draft each r in due up to 20 email to r.email subject "Your renewal date tomorrow": "Hi {r.name}, a reminder from the gym: your renewal date is tomorrow."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

procedure StableWinBack {
  about "Nudge riders whose trail ride was long ago"
  policy StablePolicy
  sheet Rides "Rides" { rider: Text, phone: Phone, ride_at: DateTime, status: Text, fee: Money, weight_notes: Text private }
  trigger every day at 11:00

  let all = fetch Rides
  let old = filter all where days_between(ride_at, today()) >= 90 and status != "cancelled"
  let oldest = sort old by ride_at first 15
  let msgs = draft each r in oldest up to 15 sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.rider default 'there'}, it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the stable."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 12 hours else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

sop:
Please set up an automation to handle customer follow-ups after orders. The automation should:

- Contact new customers immediately after they place an order.
- Wait 5 days before sending a follow-up email.
- Only send the follow-up email if the order status hasn't changed to shipped or cancelled.
- Send the follow-up email during business hours (8:00 AM to 6:00 PM).
- Limit daily sends to 50 emails.
- Ensure the owner approves both the initial contact and the follow-up email before sending.
- Send the initial contact email right away but give the owner 2 hours to approve it.
- Send the follow-up email only after the owner has approved the first one.

Could you also make sure to protect customer payment information by not revealing card notes?
policy:
policy RetailPolicy {
  allow read Orders(customer, email, status, card_note)
  allow write Orders(status)
  allow contact Orders.email
  deny reveal Orders.card_note
  limit sends 50 per day
  send only between 08:00 and 18:00
}
sheets: sheet Orders "Orders" { customer: Text, email: Email, ordered_on: Date, status: Text, total: Money, card_note: Text private }
program:
procedure RetailFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new customer, then follow up once"
  policy RetailPolicy
  sheet Orders "Orders" { customer: Text, email: Email, ordered_on: Date, status: Text, total: Money, card_note: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Orders

  let first = draft email to r.email subject "Welcome": "Hi {r.customer default 'there'}, thanks for choosing the shop! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 5 days
  let all = fetch Orders
  let now_r = find all where email == r.email else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "shipped" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft email to now_r.email subject "Checking in": "Hi {now_r.customer default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

sop:
Hi there,

I'd like to set up an automation to nudge our clients who haven't had a cleaning for over 90 days. Can you please create this automation to run every day at 5:30 PM? Here are the details:

- Fetch all entries from the "Cleanings" sheet.
- Filter out any entries where the cleaning was more than 90 days ago and the status is not "cancelled".
- Select the top 10 oldest entries.
- Draft an SMS message for each of these 10 clients: "Hi [Client Name], it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the service."
- Request batch approval from me within 6 hours. If I don't approve within this time, the process should stop.
- Only send the messages between 9 AM and 9 PM.

Thanks for your help!

Best,
[Your Name]
policy:
policy CleaningPolicy {
  allow read Cleanings(client, phone, scheduled, status, door_code)
  allow contact Cleanings.phone
  deny reveal Cleanings.door_code
  limit sends 150 per day
  send only between 09:00 and 21:00
  approval batch valid 2 hours max 10 preview 5
}
sheets: sheet Cleanings "Cleanings" { client: Text, phone: Phone, scheduled: DateTime, status: Text, fee: Money, door_code: Text private }
program:
procedure CleaningWinBack {
  about "Nudge clients whose cleaning was long ago"
  policy CleaningPolicy
  sheet Cleanings "Cleanings" { client: Text, phone: Phone, scheduled: DateTime, status: Text, fee: Money, door_code: Text private }
  trigger every day at 17:30

  let all = fetch Cleanings
  let old = filter all where days_between(scheduled, today()) >= 90 and status != "cancelled"
  let oldest = sort old by scheduled first 10
  let msgs = draft each r in oldest up to 10 sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.client default 'there'}, it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the service."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

Hi Assistant,

Could you please set up an automation for following up with new clients? Here are the details:

- When a new client is added, send them a welcome SMS saying, "Hi [Client Name], thanks for choosing the salon! Reply with any questions."
- After 2 days, send another SMS asking, "Hi [Client Name], just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?" Only send this if their status hasn't changed to "lapsed" or "cancelled."
- Please get my approval before sending both messages.
- The first message should be sent within 12 hours of receiving the request.
- The entire process must be completed between 8:00 AM and 6:00 PM daily.
- No more than 150 messages can be sent in a day.

Thank you!

Best,
[Owner's Name]
policy:
policy SalonPolicy {
  allow read Clients(name, phone, status)
  allow write Clients(status)
  allow contact Clients.phone
  deny reveal Clients.color_formula
  limit sends 150 per day
  send only between 08:00 and 18:00
}
sheets: sheet Clients "Clients" { name: Text, phone: Phone, last_visit: Date, status: Text, tab: Money, color_formula: Text private }
program:
procedure SalonFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new client, then follow up once"
  policy SalonPolicy
  sheet Clients "Clients" { name: Text, phone: Phone, last_visit: Date, status: Text, tab: Money, color_formula: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Clients

  let first = draft sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.name default 'there'}, thanks for choosing the salon! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 12 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 2 days
  let all = fetch Clients
  let now_r = find all where phone == r.phone else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "lapsed" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft sms to now_r.phone: "Hi {now_r.name default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 12 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

sop:
Could you please set up an automation for following up with new customers after a few days? Here are the details:

- When a new order is placed, send an initial message saying, "Hi [Customer Name], thanks for choosing our store! Reply with any questions."
- Wait for 3 days.
- Then send a follow-up message, "Hi [Customer Name], just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
- Only send these messages between 9:00 AM and 9:00 PM daily.
- Only allow up to 50 messages per day.
- Only the owner should approve each message within 12 hours; otherwise, the automation stops.
- The follow-up message should only be sent if the customer hasn't installed the tank or cancelled the order yet.
- Do not disclose any sensitive information like home access details.

Thanks!
policy:
policy AquariumPolicy {
  allow read TankOrders(customer, phone, status, home_access)
  allow write TankOrders(status)
  allow contact TankOrders.phone
  deny reveal TankOrders.home_access
  limit sends 50 per day
  send only between 09:00 and 21:00
}
sheets: sheet TankOrders "TankOrders" { customer: Text, phone: Phone, install_on: Date, status: Text, price: Money, home_access: Text private }
program:
procedure AquariumFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new customer, then follow up once"
  policy AquariumPolicy
  sheet TankOrders "TankOrders" { customer: Text, phone: Phone, install_on: Date, status: Text, price: Money, home_access: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in TankOrders

  let first = draft sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.customer}, thanks for choosing the store! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 12 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 3 days
  let all = fetch TankOrders
  let now_r = find all where phone == r.phone else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "installed" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft sms to now_r.phone: "Hi {now_r.customer default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 12 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

  allow contact Rentals.phone

sheets: sheet Rentals "Rentals" { renter: Text, phone: Phone, due_back: Date, status: Text, deposit: Money, id_number: Text private }
program:
procedure CostumeWinBack {
  about "Nudge renters whose return date was long ago"
  policy CostumePolicy
  sheet Rentals "Rentals" { renter: Text, phone: Phone, due_back: Date, status: Text, deposit: Money, id_number: Text private }
  trigger every tuesday at 16:00

  let all = fetch Rentals
  let old = filter all where days_between(due_back, today()) >= 42 and status != "cancelled"

  let msgs = draft each r in oldest up to 10 sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.renter default 'there'}, it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the shop."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "batch not approved"

  about "Nudge guests whose reservation was long ago"
  policy RestaurantPolicy
  sheet Bookings "Bookings" { guest: Text, phone: Phone, at: DateTime, status: Text, deposit: Money, allergies: Text private }
  trigger every day at 18:00

  policy PestPolicy
  sheet Treatments "Treatments" { customer: Text, phone: Phone, treat_on: Date, status: Text, price: Money, pet_notes: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Treatments

procedure PrintshopWinBack {
  about "Nudge customers whose print job was long ago"
  policy PrintshopPolicy
  sheet Jobs "Jobs" { customer: Text, email: Email, due: Date, status: Text, quote: Money, file_link: Text private }

  let old = filter all where days_between(due, today()) >= 30 and status != "cancelled"

  let msgs = draft each r in oldest up to 20 email to r.email subject "We miss you": "Hi {r.customer default 'there'}, it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the shop."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

- When a new student signs up (new row in the Passes sheet), send them a welcome email.

- The follow-up email also needs the owner’s approval within 6 hours.
- Limit the number of emails sent to 200 per day.
- Only send emails between 7:30 AM and 7:00 PM.
- Do not include any sensitive information like injury notes.
- Ensure the owner is notified after both emails are sent.

Thank you!

  allow read Passes(name, email, status)
  allow write Passes(status)
  allow contact Passes.email
  deny reveal Passes.injury_notes
  limit sends 200 per day

program:
procedure YogaFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new student, then follow up once"
  policy YogaPolicy
  sheet Passes "Passes" { name: Text, email: Email, expires_on: Date, status: Text, credit: Money, injury_notes: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Passes

  let first = draft email to r.email subject "Welcome": "Hi {r.name}, thanks for choosing the studio! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 3 days
  let all = fetch Passes
  let now_r = find all where email == r.email else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "expired" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft email to now_r.email subject "Checking in": "Hi {now_r.name}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 6 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

sop: Could you set up an automation to nudge skaters who haven't visited for a long time? It should run daily at 4:00 PM and target skaters whose last session was over 42 days ago, unless their status is marked as "cancelled". The system should send up to 10 nudging emails each day, with a limit of 200 emails per day. Emails should be sent between 9:00 AM and 9:00 PM. Each email should be drafted and previewed for no more than 2 hours, and the owner needs to approve batches of emails within a 12-hour window; otherwise, the automation should halt. Only the skater's name and session details should be visible, and no personal health information should be disclosed. Can you please handle this?
policy:
policy IcerinkPolicy {
  allow read Skaters(skater, email, session_at, status)
  allow contact Skaters.email
  deny reveal Skaters.medical_info
  limit sends 200 per day
  send only between 09:00 and 21:00
  approval batch valid 2 hours max 10 preview 5
}
sheets: sheet Skaters "Skaters" { skater: Text, email: Email, session_at: DateTime, status: Text, fee: Money, medical_info: Text private }
program:
procedure IcerinkWinBack {
  about "Nudge skaters whose skate session was long ago"
  policy IcerinkPolicy
  sheet Skaters "Skaters" { skater: Text, email: Email, session_at: DateTime, status: Text, fee: Money, medical_info: Text private }
  trigger every day at 16:00

  let all = fetch Skaters
  let old = filter all where days_between(session_at, today()) >= 42 and status != "cancelled"
  let oldest = sort old by session_at first 10
  let msgs = draft each r in oldest up to 10 email to r.email subject "We miss you": "Hi {r.skater}, it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the rink."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 12 hours else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}

program:
procedure CleaningFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new client, then follow up once"
  policy CleaningPolicy
  sheet Cleanings "Cleanings" { client: Text, phone: Phone, scheduled: DateTime, status: Text, fee: Money, door_code: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Cleanings

  let first = draft sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.client}, thanks for choosing the service! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 2 days
  let all = fetch Cleanings
  let now_r = find all where phone == r.phone else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "done" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft sms to now_r.phone: "Hi {now_r.client default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}

  allow read Jobs(owner_name, phone, promised, status, vin)
  allow contact Jobs.phone

program:
procedure AutorepairWinBack {
  about "Nudge customers whose pickup time was long ago"
  policy AutorepairPolicy
  sheet Jobs "Jobs" { owner_name: Text, phone: Phone, promised: DateTime, status: Text, estimate: Money, vin: Text private }
  trigger every day at 09:00

  let all = fetch Jobs
  let old = filter all where days_between(promised, today()) >= 60 and status != "cancelled"
  let oldest = sort old by promised first 10
  let msgs = draft each r in oldest up to 10 sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.owner_name default 'there'}, it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the shop."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}
